title: Research Publication: Multispectral Drone for Faster and More Precise Monitoring of Papaya Plant Health

body:
Yogyakarta, May 15, 2026 – Smart Agriculture Research Center Universitas Gadjah Mada has produced another research publication in the international journal **Agricultural Environment and Sustainability** published by Elsevier. This research develops an approach for monitoring papaya plant health using multispectral UAV-VTOL imagery and Artificial Intelligence (AI) analysis.

Papaya is one of the important tropical horticultural commodities; however, its health condition can vary across a single field. These differences can be influenced by water availability, nutrient content, soil conditions, and microenvironments surrounding the plants. To date, plant health monitoring has often been conducted through visual observation or direct field measurements, which require considerable time and labor.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/799-1-image-25-1030x393.webp)

The research entitled **"Predicting Physiological Health States of Tropical Papaya Using UAV Multispectral Imagery for Precision Agriculture Monitoring"** was conducted by **Ardan Wiratmoko, Andri Prima Nugroho, Mutiara Alifia Ramadhanty, Fahmi Arsyad, Fadel Arya Pradana, Bondan Satria Pamungkas, Lilik Sutiarso, and Takashi Okayasu**. The article has been available online since **May 15, 2026** with article number **100023**.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/799-2-image-26-1030x654.webp)

The research was conducted on **103 papaya trees** in a commercial plantation in Yogyakarta. The research team used a VTOL drone equipped with a multispectral sensor to record the plant canopy conditions from the air. At the same time, physiological measurements of plants were also conducted in the field, such as chlorophyll content, stomatal activity, and plant photosynthesis indicators.

Through data analysis, the health condition of papaya plants was classified into three categories: **Healthy**, **Moderate**, and **Stressed**. These three categories were not determined solely by the visual appearance of plants, but based on a combination of plant physiological data. Thus, this system can help recognize plant conditions in a more objective and data-driven manner.

Drone data was then analyzed using a **Random Forest** model to predict plant health categories. From 124 spectral features generated from drone imagery, the model filtered important features down to 21 main features. As a result, the model achieved a test accuracy of **90.3%** and cross-validation accuracy of **0.96 ± 0.02**.

## **Collaboration and Support:**

This research was conducted through collaboration between Smart Agriculture Research Center, Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada, and the Department of Agro-Environmental Sciences, Kyushu University, Japan. This collaboration brought together expertise in precision agriculture, UAV-based remote sensing, plant physiology, data analysis, and plant monitoring decision support systems for tropical horticultural crops.

This research also received funding support from the Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada through the FTP Innovative Research Grant Batch 1 Year 2025. Smart Agriculture Research Center UGM provided technical support in field data acquisition activities and UAV operations, while the Inter-University Excellence Center (PUAPT) UGM WGFS 1.2 Precision Agriculture and Smart Farming supported access to research facilities. The research team also extends appreciation to Samuel Gatot Marseno, Hafidz Ebril Perdana, and Lukas Wiku Kuswidiyanto for their assistance in field measurements and data collection.

## **Benefits and Impact:**

This research demonstrates that multispectral drones can be an effective tool for monitoring papaya plant health in a faster, broader, and more precise manner. This technology has the potential to help farmers, plantation managers, and researchers identify plant areas that require early attention, so that field observation activities can be conducted in a more targeted manner.

With this approach, plants in healthy condition can be monitored routinely, plants in moderate condition can be prioritized for field inspection, while plants showing signs of stress can be examined further immediately. This information can support decision-making regarding irrigation, fertilization, and land management in a more appropriate manner.

From a sustainability perspective, this research aligns with several Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). More precise plant health monitoring can support SDG 2: Zero Hunger through improved productivity and resilience of food production systems. The use of UAVs, multispectral sensors, and Artificial Intelligence also supports SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure through the development of agricultural technology innovations. Furthermore, the use of data for more appropriate irrigation and fertilization management also supports SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production, as it can help reduce wastage of resources and agricultural inputs. In the long term, this data-driven plant monitoring system also contributes to SDG 13: Climate Action, particularly in helping farmers adapt to changing environmental and climatic conditions.

Going forward, this technology has the potential to be developed as part of a precision agriculture system for tropical horticulture. Integration of UAV-VTOL, multispectral sensors, physiological measurements, and artificial intelligence can help improve the efficiency of plantation management, reduce delays in detecting plant stress, and support more sustainable agricultural production.

The complete publication of this research can be accessed through the following DOI link: [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ages.2026.100023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ages.2026.100023)

**Contact:** Ardan Wiratmoko, S.T.P., M.Sc. ardan.w@ugm.ac.id

original.body:
Yogyakarta, 15 Mei 2026 – Smart Agriculture Research Center Universitas Gadjah Mada kembali menghasilkan publikasi penelitian di jurnal internasional **Agricultural Environment and Sustainability** yang diterbitkan oleh Elsevier. Penelitian ini mengembangkan pendekatan pemantauan kesehatan tanaman pepaya menggunakan citra UAV-VTOL multispektral dan analisis Artificial Intelligence (AI).

Tanaman pepaya merupakan salah satu komoditas hortikultura tropis yang penting, namun kondisi kesehatannya dapat berbeda-beda dalam satu lahan. Perbedaan ini dapat dipengaruhi oleh ketersediaan air, unsur hara, kondisi tanah, maupun lingkungan mikro di sekitar tanaman. Selama ini, pemantauan kesehatan tanaman sering dilakukan melalui pengamatan visual atau pengukuran langsung di lapangan, yang membutuhkan waktu dan tenaga cukup besar.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/799-1-image-25-1030x393.webp)

Penelitian yang berjudul **“Predicting Physiological Health States of Tropical Papaya Using UAV Multispectral Imagery for Precision Agriculture Monitoring”** ini dilakukan oleh **Ardan Wiratmoko, Andri Prima Nugroho, Mutiara Alifia Ramadhanty, Fahmi Arsyad, Fadel Arya Pradana, Bondan Satria Pamungkas, Lilik Sutiarso, dan Takashi Okayasu**. Artikel ini telah tersedia secara online pada **15 Mei 2026** dengan nomor artikel **100023**.   

![](/brand/uploads/notes/799-2-image-26-1030x654.webp)

Penelitian dilakukan pada **103 pohon pepaya** di lahan perkebunan komersial di Yogyakarta. Tim peneliti menggunakan drone VTOL yang dilengkapi sensor multispektral untuk merekam kondisi kanopi tanaman dari udara. Pada saat yang sama, pengukuran fisiologis tanaman juga dilakukan di lapangan, seperti kandungan klorofil, aktivitas stomata, dan indikator fotosintesis tanaman.

Melalui analisis data, kondisi tanaman pepaya dikelompokkan menjadi tiga kategori, yaitu **Healthy**, **Moderate**, dan **Stressed**. Ketiga kategori ini tidak ditentukan hanya dari tampilan visual tanaman, tetapi berdasarkan kombinasi data fisiologis tanaman. Dengan demikian, sistem ini dapat membantu mengenali kondisi tanaman secara lebih objektif dan berbasis data.

Data drone kemudian dianalisis menggunakan model **Random Forest** untuk memprediksi kategori kesehatan tanaman. Dari 124 fitur spektral yang dihasilkan dari citra drone, model menyaring fitur-fitur terpenting hingga menjadi 21 fitur utama. Hasilnya, model mampu mencapai akurasi pengujian sebesar **90,3%** dan akurasi validasi silang sebesar **0,96 ± 0,02**.

## **Kolaborasi dan Dukungan:**

Penelitian ini terlaksana melalui kolaborasi antara Smart Agriculture Research Center, Departemen Teknik Pertanian dan Biosistem, Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian, Universitas Gadjah Mada, dengan Department of Agro-Environmental Sciences, Kyushu University, Jepang. Kolaborasi ini mempertemukan keahlian dalam bidang pertanian presisi, penginderaan jauh berbasis UAV, fisiologi tanaman, analisis data, dan sistem pendukung keputusan untuk pemantauan tanaman hortikultura tropis.

Penelitian ini juga mendapatkan dukungan pendanaan dari Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian, Universitas Gadjah Mada melalui Hibah Penelitian Inovatif FTP Batch 1 Tahun 2025. Smart Agriculture Research Center UGM memberikan dukungan teknis dalam kegiatan akuisisi data lapangan dan operasional UAV, sedangkan Pusat Unggulan Antar Perguruan Tinggi (PUAPT) UGM WGFS 1.2 Precision Agriculture and Smart Farming mendukung akses fasilitas penelitian. Tim peneliti juga menyampaikan apresiasi kepada Samuel Gatot Marseno, Hafidz Ebril Perdana, dan Lukas Wiku Kuswidiyanto atas bantuan dalam pengukuran lapangan dan pengumpulan data.

## **Manfaat dan Dampak:**

Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa drone multispektral dapat menjadi alat bantu yang efektif untuk memantau kesehatan tanaman pepaya secara lebih cepat, luas, dan presisi. Teknologi ini berpotensi membantu petani, pengelola kebun, dan peneliti dalam mengenali area tanaman yang membutuhkan perhatian lebih awal, sehingga kegiatan pengamatan lapangan dapat dilakukan secara lebih terarah.

Dengan pendekatan ini, tanaman yang berada dalam kondisi sehat dapat dipantau secara rutin, tanaman dengan kondisi sedang dapat diprioritaskan untuk pengecekan lapangan, sedangkan tanaman yang terindikasi stres dapat segera diperiksa lebih lanjut. Informasi tersebut dapat mendukung pengambilan keputusan terkait irigasi, pemupukan, dan manajemen lahan secara lebih tepat.

Dari sisi keberlanjutan, penelitian ini sejalan dengan beberapa tujuan Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Pemantauan kesehatan tanaman yang lebih presisi dapat mendukung SDG 2: Zero Hunger melalui peningkatan produktivitas dan ketahanan sistem produksi pangan. Penggunaan UAV, sensor multispektral, dan Artificial Intelligence juga mendukung SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure melalui pengembangan inovasi teknologi pertanian. Selain itu, pemanfaatan data untuk pengelolaan irigasi dan pemupukan yang lebih tepat turut mendukung SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production, karena dapat membantu mengurangi pemborosan sumber daya dan input pertanian. Dalam jangka panjang, sistem pemantauan tanaman berbasis data ini juga berkontribusi pada SDG 13: Climate Action, khususnya dalam membantu petani beradaptasi terhadap perubahan kondisi lingkungan dan iklim.

Ke depan, teknologi ini berpeluang dikembangkan sebagai bagian dari sistem pertanian presisi untuk hortikultura tropis. Integrasi UAV-VTOL, sensor multispektral, pengukuran fisiologis, dan kecerdasan buatan dapat membantu meningkatkan efisiensi pengelolaan kebun, mengurangi keterlambatan deteksi stres tanaman, serta mendukung produksi pertanian yang lebih berkelanjutan.

Publikasi lengkap penelitian ini dapat diakses melalui tautan DOI berikut: [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ages.2026.100023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ages.2026.100023)
